'''Katharina Theresia Huber''' (born 1965){{r|born}} is a German applied mathematician and mathematical biologist whose research concerns [[phylogenetic tree]]s, [[Phylogenetics|evolutionary analysis]], their mathematical foundations, and their [[mathematical visualization]]. She is an associate professor in the School of Computing Sciences at the [[University of East Anglia]] in England, and the school's director of postgraduate research.{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Huber completed a doctorate in mathematics at [[Bielefeld University]] in 1997. Her dissertation, ''A T-theoretical Approach to Phylogenetic Analysis and Cluster Analysis'', was jointly supervised by [[Andreas Dress]] and Walter Deuber.{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at [[Massey University]] in New Zealand, Huber became a lecturer in mathematics at [[Mid Sweden University]] in [[Sundsvall]], Sweden in 2000. She moved to the Department of Biometry and Engineering of the [[Uppsala University]] in Sweden in 2003, and to the School of Computing Sciences at the University of East Anglia in 2004, where she became a senior lecturer in 2012.{{r|profile}}

==Contributions==
Huber is a coauthor of the book ''Basic Phylogenetic Combinatorics'' (Cambridge University Press, 2012),{{r|bpc}} and a codeveloper of the ape package for evolutionary analysis in [[R (programming language)|the R statistical programming system]].{{r|ape}}
